offered_action_specs.name: rollback_deploy
offered_action_specs.description: Roll one service back to the settings it ran before its latest deploy, as the deploy log records them. Code plans it from that log, not from your tools' results, so you can name it even when they cannot see deploys: if the log holds no deploy of that service to undo, or the service changed since, code refuses it. Its container is recreated, so the service pauses while it restarts. Money already booked wrong stays wrong: a rollback stops new damage, and repairs nothing.

proposed.why: The money check shows every charge since pmt_000231 at exactly 100x our amount. The deploy log shows payments-api was redeployed with CHARGE_AMOUNT_UNIT=dollars seconds before the alert, which explains it.

diagnosis.hypothesis: payments-api was redeployed at 16:57:59Z with CHARGE_AMOUNT_UNIT=dollars. Our amounts are stored in cents, so payments-api now sends the provider a cents value that the provider reads in its own unit. Every charge since then has come out at exactly 100x our recorded amount (for example, pmt_000231 is $19.32 in our records but $1,932.00 at the provider). That breaks payments_match_provider. The ledger books the provider's amounts from webhooks, so ledger_balanced and matches_provider still pass, but our payment records disagree with the provider. One payment (pmt_000233) is still pending on our side but already charged at the provider. That is likely in-flight timing, though it may also be a side effect of the unit change. Charges before pmt_000231 match. What remains open: I did not confirm the outbound request body in logs or traces, and the deploy log does not show the setting's value before this deploy.

evidence.shows: payments_match_provider fails with 59 findings starting at pmt_000231. Each provider charge is exactly 100x our amount_cents (1932 vs 193200, 14312 vs 1431200, and so on). The other four invariants pass, so the damage is limited to charge amounts.
payments-api was redeployed at 16:57:59Z, about 17s before the alert, with CHARGE_AMOUNT_UNIT=dollars. It is the only service changed after the 16:56:32Z stack start.

proposed_fix.summary: Roll payments-api back to its pre-16:57:59Z settings so charge amounts are sent in the unit the provider expects. Then refund or adjust with the provider the excess on the roughly 59 overcharged payments from pmt_000231 onward. Correct the ledger, which booked the inflated amounts, through a data repair. Resolve pmt_000233's pending state.

diagnosis.blast_radius: payments-api pauses while its container is recreated, so payment and refund requests fail or retry for a few seconds. The rollback does not repair the charges already inflated at the provider or the ledger entries booked from them. Those need a separate refund and data repair. Synthetic data only.
diagnosis.rollback_plan: If the rollback makes things worse, redeploy payments-api with the 16:57:59Z settings (CHARGE_AMOUNT_UNIT=dollars, PROVIDER_BREAKER=on, REFUND_CONNECTION=returned). Then rerun the money check to confirm which state is correct.
